text: You can't fix this system. You have to break it.
followUp: Name the last time a system fixed itself from the inside.

text: A revolution usually costs more than it wins.
You could vote your way to a completely different economy.
followUp: If it were possible, why hasn't anyone done it?

text: Capitalism will eventually collapse on its own.
followUp: And if it doesn't? What's the backup plan?

text: Violence is acceptable if what it builds is good.
followUp: Who gets to decide it was good — the people who did it, or the people it happened to?

text: Tax the rich hard enough and inequality goes away.
When every peaceful option is gone, an uprising is justified.
followUp: Who certifies that the options are actually gone?

text: Factories and farms should belong to everyone, not to someone.
Giving workers a vote at work is enough. You don't need to change who owns it.
Today's social democrats sold out everything the left stood for.
People's politics come from their bank balance, not their beliefs.
followUp: Then explain everyone who votes against their own wallet.

text: History is mostly one class fighting another.
History gets moved by individuals and ideas, not forces.
Everyone gives what they can. Everyone gets what they need.
followUp: Who assesses what you can give?

text: Complete equality is actually achievable, not just a nice idea.
A poor country has to get rich before it can get fair.
The powerful can be talked into giving up power peacefully.
Big change happens slowly or it doesn't last.
Economies run better built from the bottom up.
People who live in a place plan it better than people who don't.
A computer could run an economy better than a market can.
followUp: Would you accept its answer if you disagreed with it?

text: A country in a hurry needs a plan, not a market.
Workplaces should be run by the people working in them.
The state is just whoever holds the monopoly on violence.
An economy run entirely from the top isn't socialism. It's the state playing boss.
Central planning always ends in paperwork.
The government should be able to assign you your job.
followUp: For a year? For life? Who signs off?

text: Getting somewhere better requires a period of rule by one side.
followUp: How do you tell a transition from a regime?

text: One world government. Good idea, badly executed — or bad idea?
Patriotism has no place on the left.
No foreign government should get a say in another country's laws.
followUp: Not even to stop something you'd call a crime?

text: Borders between friendly countries should just be open.
A country that believes in something should spread it abroad.
You have more in common with a worker abroad than with your own boss.
Every people should get to decide its own future.
followUp: Including the ones whose decision you'd hate?

text: I'd accept being poorer so another country could be less poor.
followUp: How much poorer, exactly?

text: Cultures that resemble each other should govern together.
Radicals should still run for office.
followUp: Has anyone ever come back out of parliament unchanged?

text: Society should be built out of workplaces, not constituencies.
followUp: So who speaks for everyone without a job?

text: Any party that leads a movement ends up ruling it.
Nothing big gets won without a mass party behind it.
A crowd that shows up on its own beats a plan drawn up in a meeting.
Movements work better loose and leaderless.
Unions got bought a long time ago.
People keep voting for parties that harm them. That tells you parties are over.
Climate is the one fight that outranks every other fight.
No climate policy is worth a real drop in how people live.
followUp: Whose living standard did you picture — yours?

text: Renewables will never fully replace fossil fuels.
End industrial farming, even if it means growing less food.
Lab-grown meat is worth serious public money.
Scrap private cars. Make transport free instead.
People should accept real hardship to keep nature intact.
followUp: Which people, and who asks them?

text: What we eat has to change completely, not slightly.
There are too many of us for the planet to carry.
followUp: Which of us did you have in mind?

text: Wrecking a bit of nature is fine if enough people gain from it.
The only way out is to live much more simply than we do.
Every big state that promised a better world trashed the environment doing it.
How a country treats queer people is a front-line political issue, not a side one.
The idea that some jobs are women's work has to die.
Marriage is a leftover from a system of ownership. Phase it out.
Abortion should be restricted.
Religion does more good than harm and should keep its influence.
Some groups should have legal protections that others don't get.
followUp: For how long, and who decides when it stops?

text: A government should never touch a religious or cultural tradition.
followUp: Not even one it considers harmful?

text: Prisons should be abolished.
followUp: Start with the person you'd least like released.

text: Letting large numbers of people immigrate is naive.
You can't fix the economy without also fixing the culture.
